rgb: The view shows a tiled entrance area directly facing a closed wooden double door fitted with metal grilles and a central latch, approximately 0.8 to 1.2 metres ahead of the camera wearer. Because the camera points sharply downward, the wearer’s lower legs, white shoes, and left hand holding a phone appear along the bottom edge; a green net is also partly visible in the lower-right corner of frames 1 and 2. Their head and upper shoulders extend beyond the frame’s top edge, while the threshold and the wearer’s raised right hand partly block their lower legs.
depth: The depth image depicts a confined entrance passage with closed double wooden doors immediately ahead of the camera wearer, around 0.5–1.0 m away at eye height, and a low cabinet on the right approximately 0.6–1.2 m distant. Both are positioned above a tiled floor about 1.5–1.7 m below the head-mounted camera, with the wearer’s legs and shoes visible along the bottom. During frames 2 and 3, the wearer’s right arm projects forward from the lower right at less than 0.3 m toward the metal door latch, which is 0.5–0.7 m away, partly blocking the right-hand door panel and the cabinet. The arm pulls back in frame 4 while the wearer moves somewhat nearer to the upper sections of the doors. In frame 5, both door panels open inward to the left and right, surrounding a second person who stands in the threshold approximately 1.0–1.5 m ahead and 0.4 m behind the wearer’s raised right hand; the top boundary crops out that person’s head. Relative to the RGB sequence, the depth rendering distinctly separates the foreground lifted arm from the cabinet and the floor shadow without uncertainty from illumination. However, it becomes unreliable in frames 3 and 4, where the upper door panels are over-saturated and appear closer than the floor, and in frame 5, where the open doorway and the standing person’s legs merge into a dark far-depth area with poor differentiation.
segmentation: Instance segmentation fails entirely in frame 1 and produces a fully black mask. In frame 2, it labels the camera wearer’s outstretched right arm on the right, roughly 0.3–0.6 m away, the right leg at bottom center, about 1.2–1.5 m below the camera, and the left hand holding an object at bottom left as distinct `person` instances. At the same time, it incorrectly classifies the closed left door panel ahead, approximately 0.8–1.0 m away, as a `chair`, and labels the right cabinet together with the right door, around 0.6–1.2 m away and 0.2 m to the right of the door seam, as a `laptop`. In frame 3, one `person` mask joins the wearer’s extended right arm, which reaches the latch 0.5 m away and within arm’s reach, to the lower leg at the bottom. Frame 4 retains only the wearer’s lower leg at bottom center after the arm withdraws from view. In frame 5, once the doors open to opposite sides, a single connected `person` mask combines the wearer’s raised right arm in the foreground with the newly revealed second person standing upright ahead, roughly 1.0–1.5 m away and facing the wearer, whose head and feet are obscured by the top border and the wearer’s hand. Although frames 2–5 help distinguish human limbs from RGB floor clutter and shadows, the segmentation is very unreliable: it omits every door, shoe, and wall in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, badly misidentifies the door and cabinet in frame 2, and fuses two separate people at different depths into one frame-5 instance.
pose: No pose information appears in frames 1–4: the map detects neither body nor hand skeletons for the camera wearer’s visible lower legs, left hand, or extended right arm as it reaches the door latch within arm’s reach at 0.5–0.7 m. Once the double doors open in frame 5, a yellow incomplete body skeleton is detected in the upper-right quadrant on the second person standing between the open door panels around 1.0–1.5 m in front of the wearer. A magenta hand skeleton also appears immediately below it, approximately 0.5–0.8 m away. The yellow landmarks follow the standing person’s left and right wrists and hips, separated horizontally by about 0.3–0.4 m, verifying that their torso faces directly toward the camera wearer while both arms hang downward within reach of the door edges. Because their head and shoulders are cropped beyond the upper edge, their gaze direction remains unobservable. Beneath the standing person’s hip level, the magenta skeleton identifies the wearer’s elevated right hand, positioned roughly 0.4–0.5 m in front of the other person’s legs and partly covering their feet. Its finger articulation is easier to discern than in the motion-blurred RGB image. Even so, the pose output is unreliable because it misses every limb in frames 1–4 and incorrectly adds isolated yellow body points to the wearer’s hand in frame 5.
